notes.body: In Japanese she says bōya, a familiar call most often used for a small boy. The story has already said the child is a girl, and both parents keep using it.
Bowls, a teapot, an aluminium pan and a deep blue stew-pot, moved under the table out of the baby's reach, mark a poor young household of the period.
The child's cry in Japanese is uma-uma, baby talk for food being tasty. It is noise banged out with the spoon while looking at her mother, not a sentence.
The Japanese here says two years are already past, though she has just said three years since the marriage. It may count the time since the child's birth.

data.say: Prepared sparse curious-only notes on boya, household vessels, baby babble and the two-years arithmetic, leaving the vision unresolved.
